title: 1985 AHSME Problem 22
statement: In a circle with center \(O,\) \(AD\) is a diameter, \(ABC\) is a chord, \(BO=5\) and \(\angle ABO=\widehat{CD}=60^\circ.\) Then the length of \(BC\) is

solutions.text:
Arc \(CD\) gives \(\angle CAD=30^\circ.\) Since \(A,B,C\) are collinear and \(A,O,D\) are collinear, \(\angle BAO=30^\circ.\) With \(\angle ABO=60^\circ,\) triangle \(ABO\) is a \(30^\circ\)-\(60^\circ\)-\(90^\circ\) triangle. Because \(BO=5,\) we get \(AB=10\) and \(AO=5\sqrt3.\)

Also \(\angle ACD=90^\circ\) because \(AD\) is a diameter. In the \(30^\circ\)-\(60^\circ\)-\(90^\circ\) triangle \(ACD,\) the hypotenuse is \(AD=10\sqrt3,\) so \(AC=15.\) Therefore \(BC=AC-AB=5.\)

Thus the correct answer is D.
hints: Use the resulting \(30^\circ\)-\(60^\circ\)-\(90^\circ\) triangles to compare \(AB\) and \(AC\)
